agent_mechanisms.description: Diagnosis: premature convergence/stagnation under a fixed rand/1/bin with F=0.5. Evidence: across all six runs success_fraction stays moderate (0.2-0.55) yet improvement_rate is ~0.0000 and stagnation_steps climbs to 47-160 while diversity decays from ~55-58 to ~22-48; the population keeps generating accepted-but-non-improving moves, so it is drifting/contracting rather than exploiting. Failure mode: loss of directional selection pressure (rand/1/bin is too undirected) combined with shrinking diversity, so no progress is made even though trials 'succeed'. Proposed mechanism: escalate operator strength and diversity injection as stagnation grows, and raise F when diversity collapses. Falsifiable prediction: on these same seeds/functions, switching to rand/2/bin (and current-to-best/1/bin at high stagnation) plus diversity injection when diversity<30 should reduce stag_max and produce nonzero improvement_rate within the 300-FE budget compared to the fixed rand/1/bin baseline.

Diagnosis: premature convergence and stagnation due to low diversity and lack of progress. Evidence: all runs show high initial diversity (55-58) dropping to 22-47, with stagnation steps reaching 19-160 and improvement rate near zero. Success fraction is moderate (0.2-0.55) but does not lead to improvement, indicating exploration without exploitation. Failure mode: rand/1/bin with F=0.5 fails to generate improving solutions, likely because the population converges to a local optimum and the mutation strategy lacks adaptive diversity injection. Falsifiable prediction: if diversity is injected when stagnation exceeds 5 steps, then improvement rate will increase and stagnation steps will decrease in subsequent generations compared to baseline.

Diagnosis: Premature convergence with persistent stagnation (stag_max up to 160) and low success fraction (mean ~0.2-0.45) despite high initial diversity. Evidence: improvement_rate is near zero across all runs, diversity declines steadily (e.g., 55.57 to 22.42), and stagnation_steps exceed 5 frequently. Failure mode: rand/1/bin with F=0.5 lacks sufficient exploration pressure; once diversity drops, the population cannot escape local optima. Falsifiable prediction: Switching to rand/2/bin when stagnation_steps >= 5 will increase success_fraction and reduce stagnation_steps in subsequent generations compared to the baseline rand/1/bin policy.
